summary: George Berrington revisited the founder proposition with Daniel Reese and Amira Khan 12 weeks after the original session. Founders told us 'growth capital without giving up control' sounded like every minority fund. It has been replaced by a lead message on the 100-day operating plan, and the lead case study has changed from the payroll software investment to the field service software business.

discussion.keyPoints: Amira tested the proposition in 31 founder meetings. Founders assumed all growth equity was minority, so the control message did not stand out.
The 100-day operating plan and named operating partners got the strongest reaction. Daniel said three founders asked for it in writing.
The payroll software founder has started a sale process and asked not to be named publicly.

recommendations.recommendation: Lead with 'a named operating partner and a 100-day plan from day one', replacing the earlier 'growth capital without giving up control' message.
Keep three pillars but reorder: 100-day operating plan first, then Northern presence, then minority-only.
Make the field service software business, where ARR grew from £2.5m to £7m in 30 months, the lead case, replacing the payroll software case.
Keep framing the cost of waiting as losing a funding window; still no hard numbers.
Still no published point of view on selling control.

actions.action: Rewrite the founder one-pager with the new lead message
Get written approval from the field service software founder

nextFocus: Update outreach templates to the new lead message.
nextPreparation: Amira to bring the reply rates from the last 12 weeks of outreach.
